title: Day 3-13
body: Made it to mount Etna around 1:00 p.m. I was able to hitch a ride into town after about half an hour. Tried to hitchhike up to Medford unsuccessfully so ended up needing to book a shuttle from Mount Shasta. 2 hours later I made it to Medford where I stayed in a hotel before flying back to Seattle. Hopefully get back on the trail Saturday night.

title: Day 3-12
body: Deer kept harassing us all night but I put in my ear plugs and slept through it. Beautiful morning, big bonus of being up at 7,000 ft now is it feels a lot cooler. I think forecast was for another 80 plus day but in the mountains it's definitely less knock on wood. I saw some more dear and lots of chipmunk friends today. Finally found some self-service about 2 mi into my hike so I stop for 20 minutes to download some podcasts and upload some video. I thought California was supposed to be a civilized place. Where's all the cell service?Today ended up being climbing up and over mountain pass after mountain pass; way more fun than anything in Oregon 😅It ended up getting pretty stormy lately in the afternoon with lots of thunder and lightning. It did rain briefly but the real damage came from all the bushes that hang over the trail being wet; they totally drenched my pants. Fortunately it stopped shortly before I went to set up camp and I found a place under trees that didn't get too much moisture. Hopefully I won't wake up in a humidifier tomorrow.

title: Day 3-11
body: Started out with a veggie omelette, 3+ cups of coffee, and a huge plate of breakfast potatoes at the Seiad Valley Diner. Got on trail later than planned and the first 7 miles was all road 🥴 the first 2 were paved highway, next 4 paved county road, and last two gravel. I have been climbing non-stop all day, following a few rivers and streams back up into the mountains. Took a great swim under one of the many bridges across the river; the only relief from the 85 degrees heat so far today. As of 3:30 I've climbed 2935ft and looking at the map, I haven't reached the steep part yet.Ended up getting to camp right at 8pm. Final stats ended up being climbing 6027ft in 21.6 miles. This campsite is beautiful but there are 20 something deer that keep harassing me and the other hikers camping here.Did not end up with cell service once all day.

title: Day 3-10
body: Got my earliest start of the trip; on the trail by 7:33. 24 mi to seiad valley so I'm hoping to get in around 5:00 before the store closes at 7:00. Quick turnaround and then back on the trail either tonight or first thing in the morning tomorrow.So far today has been walking ridgelines, so glad to be out of the Oregon tunnel. No mosquitoes yet in California either. First thing this morning I'm walking on the left side of a ridge and the right side has cell service. Each time I peek over a pass, I get cell service for about 30 seconds and then I lose it. One of these times I need to stop and actually upload all my stuff from yesterday.

title: Day 3-9
body: Got a late start again today, on the trail around 750. Little bit of metal walking and then it's been mostly ridgelines to the California border. Even saw a cooler of trail magic and had a lukewarm Sprite. Lots of water today, making for light carries. Saw some deer, hummingbirds, cows, and some poorly behaved unleashed dogs who pooped on the trail and the owner did not bother to pick it up.Reach the California border around 1:45, did some celebrating in the form of dancing and throwing water in the air. I have now officially walked the entire length of organ on the PCT. Continuing down from the border into a big valley with no cell service only to then climb out of that same valley on the other side over Big Ridge. I was making good Pace so I thought I could maybe make it to 50k, but the sun won this round. Ended up making 28.6 mi I believe. At one point I paused my watch and missed 0.5 mi of tracking but I'm hoping I can fix that in the TCX data when I have Wi-Fi and Seiad valley. Couldn't find a great campsite but found one that did the job. I picked up some ear plugs in Ashland and those were amazing for falling asleep.

title: Day 3-8
body: Forgot to write a blog yesterday oops. Box arrived in Ashland around 11:30 and was able to get a ride up to the trailhead and start hiking around 1:00. A little over a mile into my hike I realized my water bottle with my water filter fell out of my bag and I then had to back Trace all the way to the highway where I found my bottle lying on the pavement. It must have fallen out of my bag when I got out of the car. Back on the trail I got to climb that hill again, and just keep on climbing the whole day. I ended up making it 12 mi before arriving at a good campsite around 6: 30 or 7. Great views of the sunset, and good cell service.

title: Day 3-7
body: Almost on the trail by 7:30; what a slacker. Right ankle is bothering me a lot again today I think I'm going to finally cave and switch to trail shoes in Ashland. I swear I'm the only PCT hiker in Boots. It's not even that the ankle itself hurts, it's the rubbing against the boot that is hurting. It was totally fine in flip-flops this morning.

title: Day 3-6
body: First half of the day was good old organ tunnel. Second half of the day has been super exposed Fields with sharp Bushes and blistering hot sun. I'm probably exaggerating the actual temperature but it feels hot when you haven't seen shade in over an hour.Took a nap near a dam with a waterfall to try and rest out the feet a bit today. Next water source had horses, not great for the purity of the water LOL. It's probably fine; I double filtered just to be safeI saw a couple huge jackrabbits, horses, a bunch of lizards, and a couple deer yesterday. Found an amazing campsite next to the best water source on the whole trail; it's a spring that's hooked up to a pipe that sprays so hard it's difficult to fill your bottle 😅 infinitely better than scummy horse pond. Probably my latest night to fall asleep but That's what happens when you are at a campsite with cell service 😂

title: Day 3-5
body: Got an early start, took a quick hot shower at fish lake, and then got on the trail just a tad before 7:45. First 5-10 miles were all volcanic rock which was a pain to hike over. Did not hit my goal of 12 by 12:00 but I did hit 12.15 at 12:15. Speaking of which, there was a cool hiker cabin at mile 12 where I got to chat with a couple from Germany. Second half of the day was classic Oregon tunnel; just hiking through trees with no views or ridges. I started looking for a campsite around mile 20 and none came up until 22.5ish so I'm sure my feet will make me pay the price tomorrow. 34 miles from Ashland and next resupply. I'm going to aim for another 20 tomorrow so I can cruise into town in the early afternoon Sunday.

title: Day 3-3 & 3-4
body: Minimal cell service. Eventually made it into Fish Lake around 1pm Wednesday. Made some friends with a few other hikers here and had a great time talking about the trail.Unfortunately when jumping in the lake I scraped open a blister so I decided to take a rest day here in Fish Lake. I'm going to try and get back on the trail first thing in the morning Friday; I have 56 miles into Ashland that I'm aiming to do over 3 days, two nights.

title: Day 3-2
body: I typed a whole long thing out but it got erased somehow. Good hike though I do have some blisters for me on my feet. Starting with 24 mi probably wasn't the best idea but didn't have much of a choice given Crater Lake's reluctance to let PCT hikers camp in park boundaries. Found a good campsite and was only kind of terrorized by deer and a bear but only via sound.

title: Day 3-1
body: July 20: Got a great night of sleep and got on the trail around 8:00 a.m.. very altitude desert vibes for the first 10 mi before getting into some snow patches getting up to Crater Lake. The trail definitely was a tease because on the map I could see I was right up next to the lake but the ridge and mountains kept walking The view. Eventually I got a really good look at the lake and some good photos which you can see on my Instagram. Was planning on doing 21 mi and that turned into 23.5 but I got a nice hot meal for dinner and got camp setup just as it started getting dark; one of the latest camp setups I've ever had. It was supposed to, and did, rain Sunday night and I hadn't needed to set up my rain fly since 2023 so it took longer than I'd like to admit to set up in the dark. Slightly less good sleep Sunday night, it did rain a bit but not terrible and I was able to keep everything dry. Made some friends on the trail near Crater Lake, shout out Allison and Lauren, then made some friends in the village as well, shout out Sadie, scratch, and presoak.

title: Day 3-0
body: Back on the trail; man, it feels good to be back! I am currently sitting in my tent waiting to fall asleep so I start hiking again first thing in the morning. Fairly easy flight + bus + hitchhike to get here and tomorrow I'll be entering crater Lake National Park and hike 10-20 miles depending on how I'm feeling. Excited to keep you all updated.
